lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Matchday one. The AI manager just benched the club's best player. Thirty thousand fans are booing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ninety minutes later... four-nil. The tracking data had spotted what no coach could: he'd lost half a yard of pace.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Week three. It signs a seventeen-year-old nobody's heard of, for less than the star earns in a month. He scores on his debut.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then it starts managing the game live. Two-nil down at half-time, it rewires the whole formation from the players' heart-rate data. Three goals in twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By Christmas, they're top of the league. The fans who booed? They're chanting its name.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then, in January... it sells the captain. No warning. No explanation. And in the cup final, he scores the winner. Against them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sounds far-fetched? Liverpool and Google DeepMind already built an AI that designs corner-kick tactics. And in a blind test, the club's own experts preferred its ideas nine times out of ten.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So... would you trust an AI with your club? Follow for more what-ifs.
